methodology.summary: Pollsmax runs two linked systems: (1) a polling-average model that produces a time-weighted, partisanship-adjusted mean of all polls for a race, and (2) a forecast model that blends that polling average with structural 'fundamentals' (generic ballot, presidential approval, incumbency, prior results, partisan lean/PVI, and Pollsmax's own editorial rating) into a composite margin, which is then run through 10,000-100,000 daily Monte Carlo simulations to produce win probabilities, a projected margin, and projected vote shares.
methodology.weighting: Race-page polling averages are a recency-weighted mean of all polls dated on or before each chart day, with the recency curve adapting to how many polls exist so sparse races (like this one, with only 1 poll) do not overreact to a single survey. Forecasts blend polling with fundamentals; at full poll depth (6+ polls for House) the standardized House weights are: Polling 30%, Editorial rating 40%, PVI 10%, prior House result 10%, incumbency 5%, generic ballot 2.5%, Trump approval 2.5%. Below the poll-count threshold, 'the polling share drops by five percentage points for each missing poll and the non-polling factors are rescaled proportionally.' For this specific PA-7 race (1 poll, well below the 6-poll threshold), the site's own displayed input-weight breakdown shows no separate polling-margin line at all: Trump Approval 3.6%, Generic Ballot 3.6%, Past Race Results 14.3%, Incumbency 7.1%, Partisan Lean 14.3%, Editorial Rating 57.1% (sums to 100%).
methodology.recency: 'More recent surveys receive higher weight' in the polling average. Trump approval and the generic ballot use a rolling ~28-day sample-size-weighted window rather than the race-specific recency curve.
methodology.pollster_quality: No explicit per-pollster letter grade or quality score is shown on the race, forecast, or methodology pages, and no separate 'pollster ratings' page was found linked from the site. The only pollster-side adjustment described is the partisan-sponsor tag adjustment (see house_effects).
methodology.house_effects: 'Before averaging, polls from pollsters tagged with a party sponsor, (D) or (R) in the pollster name, receive a fixed margin adjustment on the modeled values. This adjustment is applied whenever the tag is present.' Separately, when 3+ paired polls exist, Pollsmax computes 'a robust consensus margin (median Democratic minus Republican)' and downweights (but does not delete) outliers via a median-absolute-deviation (MAD) scale; with only 1 poll in this race that outlier step cannot engage.
methodology.forecast_model: The composite expected Democratic margin from the weighted blend of polling and fundamentals 'is converted to a win probability using a calibrated margin-to-odds curve, ... slightly steeper than a pure linear scale.' House races use 'a steeper House-specific curve' than Senate/governor. A Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 draws per House district daily) then draws 'from a normal distribution centered on a calibrated target margin' that 'blends the odds-implied margin from the composite win probability with the raw composite margin itself.' 'Simulation spread (sigma) is calibrated so the model's win probability matches anchor points at standard rating tiers; for example, roughly 95% for a safe seat and 75% for a likely seat.' The displayed race rating (e.g. 'Tilt D') is 'derived from the composite win probability using fixed probability breakpoints aligned with Pollsmax editorial tiers.'
quotes: Pollsmax creates a time-weighted and partisanship-adjusted polling average from an aggregate of all polls conducted for the general election.
For Senate, House, and gubernatorial general-election pages, the polling average is a recency-weighted mean of all polls dated on or before each chart day. More recent surveys receive higher weight.

Before averaging, polls from pollsters tagged with a party sponsor, (D) or (R) in the pollster name, receive a fixed margin adjustment on the modeled values. This adjustment is applied whenever the tag is present.

When at least three polls with paired Democratic and Republican toplines are available, we compute a robust consensus margin (median Democratic minus Republican) and measure each poll's distance from that consensus using a median absolute deviation (MAD) scale. Polls far from the pack receive lower weight but are not deleted.
Each forecast blends polling data with structural factors such as partisanship, incumbency, prior results, national environment indicators, and race ratings.
HOUSE (6+ POLLS): Polling 30%; editorial rating 40%; PVI 10%; prior House result 10%; incumbency 5%; generic ballot 2.5%; Trump approval 2.5%.

When poll counts fall below the full threshold, the polling share drops by five percentage points for each missing poll and the non-polling factors are rescaled proportionally so the blend still sums to 100%.

The weighted composite yields a single expected Democratic margin. That margin is converted to a win probability using a calibrated margin-to-odds curve... House races use a steeper House-specific curve.
Displayed race ratings (for example Likely D, Lean R, Tossup) are derived from the composite win probability using fixed probability breakpoints aligned with Pollsmax editorial tiers.
Simulation spread (sigma) is calibrated so the model's win probability matches anchor points at standard rating tiers; for example, roughly 95% for a safe seat and 75% for a likely seat.

ratings.note: This is Pollsmax's own composite forecast-tier rating (win-probability-derived), not an outside rating (e.g. Cook/Sabato/Inside Elections) and not a per-pollster grade. No separate pollster-rating or race-rating explainer page beyond /forecast-methodology/ and /polling-methodology/ was found linked from the target pages.

extra.race_overview_text: The 2026 Pennsylvania 7th District House election features Democrat Bob Brooks and Republican Ryan Mackenzie. Incumbent Representative Ryan Mackenzie is seeking reelection to a second term. The election for the district's House seat is rated as tilt Democratic in 2026. The race will test whether Democrats can flip a competitive Pennsylvania seat or whether Republicans can hold one of their key House battlegrounds. Pennsylvania's 7th District will be critical in determining control of the House for the second half of President Trump's term.

Because the polling average is built from a single poll, the race page renders a static bar chart rather than a Chart.js line/time-series chart ('Chart: bar when <=2 polls, line when >=3' per an HTML comment in the page source); there is therefore no separate polling-average time series beyond the single GBAO data point.

The forecast page's 'Simulated Results Distribution' histogram is drawn on a plain canvas (not Chart.js) and its underlying per-bin values could not be extracted; only the surrounding descriptive text and the current projected margin were captured.

extraction_problems: Internal inconsistency on pollsmax.com itself: the same GBAO poll is labeled 'GBAO (B)' in the embedded houseDistrictConfig JSON on both the main race page and the forecast page, and in 3 of 5 rendered DOM locations, but labeled 'GBAO (D)' in 2 other rendered DOM locations on the forecast page (a duplicate/secondary snapshot block and the forecast page's own poll table row). Per Pollsmax's own polling-methodology text, only '(D) or (R)' are documented as valid partisan-sponsor tags -- '(B)' does not match that documented scheme, so it is unclear whether '(B)' is a stray/incorrect render, a different kind of internal tag (e.g. a pollster grade), or the '(D)' instances are the stale/incorrect ones. Because of this contradiction, 'partisan' and 'sponsor' were both recorded as null rather than guessed (GBAO Strategies is publicly known as a Democratic-aligned pollster, but that external fact was not used to resolve the site's own internal inconsistency).

Similar duplicate-block inconsistency: main.html renders two 'Last updated' values for the polling average in different DOM sections -- '12:00 AM on July 2, 2026' (matching the single poll's date) and '12:00 AM on August 30, 2026' (matching the retrieval/today's date). Used the latter (today's date) for average.as_of since it appears in the primary visible snapshot block, but both values are present in the page source.

The forecast trend charts' (Projected Vote Share, Odds of Winning) most recent plotted data point is dated 2026-08-19, eleven days before this page's own 'FORECAST LAST UPDATED: 12:00 AM on August 30, 2026' headline stat and before the actual retrieval date (2026-08-30). This gap between the stated update time and the actual last chart datapoint is a site-side discrepancy, not an extraction error.

No standalone pollster-ratings/grades page (analogous to a '538 pollster ratings' page) was found linked from the swept pages; only /polling-methodology/, /forecast-methodology/, /about/, and /contact/ were discoverable as methodology/about-type pages from the target and forecast pages' navigation and footer.
No text resembling injected instructions directed at an AI/automation was found on any swept page; all content was treated as ordinary data.
